newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian sugar up on restricted arrivals, low demand.
newsitem.headline: Indian sugar up on restricted arrivals, low demand.

text.p: Sugar prices extended gains on the local market on Wednesday, dealers said.
Demand from both retailers and consumers remained slow however, but the shortage of ready stock following restricted arrivals dragged prices upward.
"Reports that the Indian government denied any proposal regarding decontrol of sugar industry for the time being also prompted speculative buying," a broker said.

"Presently the government has some control over the price of sugar as well as the release of monthly quotas but if the government announces decontrol the market will receive more free sale sugar," he said.
In ready delivery sugar S-30 rose by 25 rupees at 1,420/1,455 rupees per quintal while M-30 looked up by 5 rupees at 1,460/1,490 rupees per quintal.
Sugar mill delivery rose to 1,360/1,380 rupees per quintal from 1,360/1,375 rupees.
Local millers are witnessing higher outstation buying at the mill level which in turn has curtailed arrivals of sugar from mills to the Bombay market.
